transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Officials in Tennessee are confirming the death row in May
Christa Gail Pike survived the state's attempt to execute her last night. The state corrections
department says Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility after officials
were unable to carry out her lethal injection. Katherine Sweeney is a reporter with member
station WPL Lend. She was among the media witnesses who described what they saw to other reporters.
She lifted her head up and was looking around at one point. She said that there was a spot that
was burning and hurting and asked if that was normal. None of it was normal. I covered all the
executions last year and most of the ones this year, we haven't seen anything like it. It went
really poorly. Tennessee Governor Bob Lee has halted executions from being carried out in the
state and has ordered an outside investigation. A commercial flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made
an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia Wednesday after one of the pilots apparently stabbed the
other pilot and tried to crash the plane. NPR's Kat Lonsdorf was at the Tel Aviv airport as
passengers from that flight finally arrived. It was a chaotic scene packed with journalists
and waiting family members. The passengers slowly emerged dragging suitcases, some crying,
some smiling, and looking relieved. Some just looked really tired. There were also quite a few
families. Dan Zoller was traveling with his wife and two small kids and saw much of the incident
on board while trying to comfort his children. The pilot was stabbed. I don't know who stabbed
him but I know that three passengers threw themselves on the terrorist and captured him.
Israeli officials are calling it an attempted terrorist attack but many details are still
unknown. The suspect pilot is in custody and Saudi officials have begun an investigation.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv. The Defense Department expanding the number of universities
that have full-time Corps of Cadets programs. NPR's Alyssa Nedwardy reports on the changes
announced by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. There are currently six universities that under
federal law have Corps of Cadet programs. Hegseth is adding five more. Louisiana State University,
Liberty University, Tuskegee University, Mississippi State University, and Hillsdale
College will now be designated a "distinguished military college." A document outlining the changes
says the new programs will make sure military officers are "grounded in the Constitution,
Western Civilization, American Heritage, and the warrior ethos at a time when many traditional
commissioning sources have drifted from those foundations." This comes just a day after Hegseth
signed a memo instructing military academies to stop granting tenure to civilian faculty
because, as he put it, "civilian academic norms undermine the war fighting mission."
Alyssa Nedwardy, NPR News. This is NPR. Iran says it has received an official U.S.
response to Tehran's proposal to bring an end to the seven-month war. Foreign Minister Abbas
Araxchi presented the response at a Cabinet meeting Wednesday. President Trump rejected that latest
offer a few days ago, but Araxchi had said that Iran has not received a formal rejection.
Iran's proposal put forward last week calls on the U.S. to lift its blockade of Iranian ports in
exchange for Iran, reopening the Strait of Hormuz within a week. Britain's Prime Minister says the
U.K. authorities have strong indications that Iran was involved in an incident near an airbase in
England where U.S. forces operate, and five men were arrested over the weekend. Philip Marx reports
that British and U.S. officials are jointly investigating. Police detained the British men
all in their 20s and from London on Sunday near RAF Fairford, a base American bombers have flown
from during this year's strikes on Iran. They were held on suspicion of explosives, offenses,
and preparing an act of terrorism, then released on bail the next day. Police say three small trucks
found at the scene contained gasoline, but no explosives. Speaking to British broadcasters,
Prime Minister Andy Burnham offered little concrete information about the alleged plot
or Iran's potential involvement, adding only the investigation remains complex and serious,
and he'd share more details soon. Iran denies any role, though has previously warned that any bases
used to attack its territory would constitute legitimate targets. For NPR News, I'm Willem
Marx in London. Stocks in Europe are down and Thursday trading after Asian shares were mostly
higher. Japan's benchmark decay closed up more than 3 percent. I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.

topics.text: Christa Gail Pike survives execution attempt in Tennessee; governor halts executions and orders investigation
Commercial flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv makes emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after pilot stabbing
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth adds five universities to Corps of Cadets programs
Iran says it received official U.S. response to proposal for ending seven-month war
British Prime Minister says authorities have strong indications Iran involved in incident near English airbase
